s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of headache and vision loss with sinus inflammation and orbital involvement
salient_findings: Vision loss in the right eye for 2 days
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
No history of chronic or allergic rhinosinusitis
Diagnosed with COVID-19 three weeks prior to presentation
Developed rhinorrhea and recovered from COVID-19
Worsening right-sided headache started 1 week after COVID-19 recovery
Right eye visual acuity limited to hand-motion detection
Severe pain on ocular motion
Sinus cultures positive for Streptococcus constellatus
Elevated Serum IgG4 level

Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis with orbital involvement
Angiolymphoid Hyperplasia with Eosinophilia and orbital involvement

Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis with orbital involvement
Angiolymphoid Hyperplasia with Eosinophilia and orbital involvement
Necrotizing Sarcoid Granulomatosis with orbital involvement

shortlist.label: IgG4-related disease
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated Serum IgG4 level and dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells

shortlist.label: Orbital Apex Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Right eye visual acuity limited to hand-motion detection and severe pain on ocular motion

shortlist.label: Invasive Aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation and bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone

shortlist.label: Mucormycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Sinus cultures positive for Streptococcus constellatus and worsening right-sided headache

shortlist.label: Acute Invasive Fungal Sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of headache and vision loss with sinus inflammation and orbital involvement

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of vision loss, severe pain on ocular motion, and limited visual acuity, combined with imaging findings of bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone and extension of inflammation into the apex, are consistent with Orbital Apex Syndrome.

rejected.label: IgG4-related disease
rejected.why: While the patient has an elevated Serum IgG4 level and histopathologic findings of IgG4-positive plasma cells, the acute presentation and severity of symptoms are more consistent with an infectious or inflammatory process like Orbital Apex Syndrome.

rejected.label: Invasive Aspergillosis
rejected.why: There is no mention of Aspergillus in the sinus cultures or pathology findings, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Mucormycosis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings do not specifically suggest Mucormycosis, and the sinus cultures were positive for Streptococcus constellatus, not Mucor.

rejected.label: Acute Invasive Fungal Sinusitis
rejected.why: While the patient has sinusitis, the presence of Streptococcus constellatus in the sinus cultures and the lack of specific findings suggestive of invasive fungal infection make this diagnosis less likely.
